title: kate-session: find and load the project file for a path
summary: find_project_file walks from a file or directory up through its parents and returns the first .kateproject it finds. load_project reads that file and parses it. The window calls both when a document opens.

lane.reason: A Cursor local agent on the owner Mac codes this packet. The crate is pure Rust and builds anywhere. The backlog marks this title LOCAL so the Mac lane keeps the panes and their models together.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: find_project_file starts at start when it is a directory and at its parent otherwise, checks dir.join(".kateproject").is_file() at each level, and stops at the filesystem root. load_project reads the file with std::fs::read_to_string; an error is ProjectError::Io; the text goes to project_from_json with the path. Export both from lib.rs. The test find_project_file_walks_up builds a tempdir with .kateproject at the top holding {"name": "T"} and a nested sub/deep/f.rs, asserts find_project_file(f.rs) is the project path, that load_project of it has name T, and that a tempdir without the file gives None. Do not nest an if inside an if. When two arms return the same value, write one condition with ||. Add each new test at the end of the one test module of the file, before its closing brace; create that module when the file is new. Do not write a second mod tests. An item with no caller outside tests gets #[cfg_attr(not(test), allow(dead_code))]; the packet that adds the caller removes it. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip.

regression_tests.name: project::tests::find_project_file_walks_up
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main because find_project_file does not exist. After the change the nested file finds the top project and a bare directory finds none.
